status_summary: No law has repealed the diversity lottery, ended family-based categories beyond the immediate family or created a points system, although bills were introduced (H.R. 1241 on 2025-02-12 and H.R. 3466 on 2025-05-15), and EO 14351 (signed 2025-09-19) created a gift-based Gold Card pathway within existing employment categories (the H-1B element is in c05-07). Executive action reached the lottery: State postponed DV-2027 registration on 2025-11-05, and after the Homeland Security Secretary's 2025-12-18 announcement USCIS held diversity visa adjustment cases (2025-12-19) and State paused diversity visa issuance under guidance that State's own later cable dates 2025-12-19. On 2026-08-28 a federal court in Northern California temporarily vacated those holds for FY2026 selectee subclasses, State's cable of 2026-09-10 rescinded the diversity and immigrant visa pause guidance in full, and on 2026-09-30 the court found State's compliance less than substantial and ordered ten more days past the fiscal year to reconsider covered FY2026 refusals. On 2026-10-14 a Southern District of California court preliminarily enjoined State to run DV-2027 registration, and a same-day order on a joint motion, shown in the copy opened as an unsigned proposed order, moved the deadlines to announcement by 2026-10-29, registration opening by 2026-11-01 for thirty days and selectee notification by 2026-12-03.

timeline.event: H.R. 1241, the SAFE for America Act of 2025, was introduced; it would repeal the diversity immigrant program from 2025-10-01.

H.R. 3466, the Securing Migration, Addressing Reform, and Talent Retention Act, was introduced; by title it would create a points system, narrow family-based immigration and end the diversity visa program.
EO 14351 created a Gold Card program in which a gift of 1 million dollars (individual) or 2 million (corporate) counts as evidence for EB-1 and EB-2 categories.
State announced changes to the Diversity Visa entry process and postponed the start of DV-2027 registration.
The Homeland Security Secretary announced she was directing USCIS to pause the diversity visa program after a shooting suspect had entered through it.

USCIS placed a hold on pending Diversity Visa adjustment of status applications (PM-602-0193), and in December 2025 the State Department paused all visa issuance to Diversity Visa applicants to review screening and vetting.
timeline.source: N.D. Cal. order describing the policies

timeline.event: The State Department paused all visa issuance to diversity immigrant visa applicants, effective immediately, while applicants could still apply and attend interviews. The State page carries no date for the pause; State's own cable of 2026-09-10 dates the pause guidance 2025-12-19 (an earlier secondary account gave 2025-12-23, which no opened document confirms).

A law firm sued the Secretary of State in the Southern District of California to compel a DV-2027 registration process; a hearing was held 2026-09-24 and a ruling was set for 2026-10-14 (see that date).

The Northern District of California (Medani v. Trump) certified subclasses of FY2026 Diversity Visa selectees and temporarily vacated the USCIS hold, the State Department pause and a separate 75-country pause as to them, finding them likely arbitrary and capricious.

The State Department posted a notice (page updated 2026-08-31) that, as of 2026-08-28 and in accordance with the Medani court order, its December 2025 pause on diversity visa issuance was no longer in effect.

State cable 26 STATE 88862, filed in Medani v. Trump on 2026-09-11 (ECF 95), rescinds in full the diversity visa pause guidance (dated 2025-12-19) and the immigrant visa pause guidance (dated 2026-01-14), bars refusals under INA 221(g) based on either pause, and tells posts to identify and reconsider cases refused solely under a pause.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of State cable as filed in court (copy hosted by AILA)

timeline.event: The Northern District of California (Medani v. Trump, ECF 137) finds State's compliance with the 2026-08-28 injunction less than substantial and orders it to take reasonable steps for ten additional days past fiscal year 2026 to reconsider FY2026 applications refused solely under the diversity visa pause or the 75-country pause; it denies a request to reserve about 40,000 unused visas, grants no stay, and sets status reports three times a week and a conference for 2026-10-15.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (via Justia)

title: Merit-based immigration: repeal diversity lottery, end chain migration, top-talent visas
uncertainties: The State Department guidance page was opened on 2026-10-19. It is undated apart from its 2026-08-31 update and carries both a notice that the December 2025 pause ended under the Medani order and the original undated pause text, and its FAQ still says no diversity visas will be issued; it does not state that issuance is resuming. The State pause date now follows State's cable of 2026-09-10, which dates the pause guidance 2025-12-19; an earlier secondary account gave 2025-12-23 for the State pause and, in its summary of the Medani order, 2025-12-20, neither of which an opened document confirms; a news report of 2025-12-19 confirms the Secretary's 2025-12-18 announcement directing USCIS to pause the program and reports no State pause, so whether the State pause was formally linked to that announcement was not confirmed. The cable was read in a copy of the government's 2026-09-11 notice of filing (ECF 95) hosted by the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA), a membership association rather than a party, and the official docket copy could not be opened (the Justia docket page was blocked); the ECF 137 order on Justia confirms only that State sent a cable to all posts on the morning of 2026-09-10 (citing ECF 95-1) and describes it as directing review of refused cases; it also states that a federal court in New York vacated the immigrant visa pause on 2026-08-21, which was not otherwise checked. The USCIS hold date (2025-12-19) and memo number come from the Medani order of 2026-08-28, which was read on a news site's copy; whether the USCIS hold was formally withdrawn beyond the FY2026 subclasses was not found. The Medani supplemental relief order of 2026-09-30 (ECF 137, Justia), the Southern District of California preliminary injunction of 2026-10-14 (ECF 21, CourtListener) and the order modifying its deadlines (ECF 23, CourtListener) were opened and read; the ECF 23 copy is headed as a proposed order with a blank signature line, so its entry as granted rests on the docket as reported by an external retrieval. ECF 21 gives no reasoning and says the grant is for reasons stated on the record, which was not read. An October Medani order setting an adjudication window of 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-23 and continuing the status conference, and a government notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit filed 2026-10-14, were reported by an external retrieval only (the window order from a counsel-run messaging channel, a rejected source type) and were not opened; no Ninth Circuit docket was located. Whether State has announced DV-2027 registration was not checked; the modified announcement deadline is 2026-10-29. The DV-2027 suit's 2026-08-19 filing and 2026-09-24 hearing come from one news article. The stage is a judgment call: blocked reflects that the executive steps counted as progress were vacated, rescinded or enjoined, while the Gold Card order (EO 14351), whose legal status was not re-checked, is treated as outside the merit-based recommendation because it rests on a payment rather than merit. The H.R. 3466 description rests on its full title. A federal lawsuit over the Gold Card filed 2026-02-03 was seen only on a law-firm site and is not relied on. No bill ending chain migration other than H.R. 3466 was checked, and the RAISE Act was not found in this Congress. The State rule of 2026-03-11 on passport information and the 75-country pause are covered in c06-05.
